newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.S. Pataki advances aid for schools, counties.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.S. Pataki advances aid for schools, counties.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki, seeking to head off criticism that school districts again will have to take out costly, short-term loans because Albany's budget will be late, advanced $65 million of aid.

"Schools need the access to state aid to ensure that books and supplies can be bought as we enter the last three months of the school year," Pataki said, in prepared remarks. The accelerated payment moves aid to March from September.

The capital last week agreed to a six-week interim budget, signalling the state again was likely to miss approving a budget by the April 1 deadline, for the 13th time in a row. Pataki told reporters in Albany: "I think it's very unfortunate and I think it just shows how difficult it has been to try to negotiate."

Asked whether he again would use pressure tactics to get his budget approved, he replied he would insist that New York State not lose its momentum on welfare reform and tax cuts. A spring snowstorm in Albany interfered with working groups' efforts on Monday, he added.
The governor also directed the Department of Social Services to send the state's counties $22 million that can be used to help people find jobs or cut local taxes.

Pataki, who attributed the state's ability to pay the counties to his Administration's success in trimming the welfare rolls, took the opportunity to press the Assembly to approve welfare reforms, saying Albany was at risk of losing hundreds of millions of dollars in federal aid if the house failed to negotiate a plan in good faith. Under the new, federal law, states must enact programs by July 1.

The Assembly was scheduled to unveil its new welfare plan on Tuesday, which was expected to reject the governor's proposal for sliding cuts in welfare benefits, though it would go along with new time limits and work requirements which they would be defined more widely to cover education.

"We must continue to reform the failed welfare system and break the cycle of government dependency that has trapped far too many," Pataki said, in remarks which stressed his plan's emphasis on work incentives.
He also approved a $25 million payment for the Roswell Park Cancer Institute to help with its "longstanding" fiscal deficit.
